primitives.name: Will Effort vs Eye Movement
primitives.verbatim_quote: The act of will produced absolutely no effect beyond the nervous system, and yet we judge of the direction of the line of vision as if the will had exercised its normal effects.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W': 'dimensionless effort of will', 'M': 'muscle activation (dimensionless)', 'D': 'perceived visual direction (degrees)'}
primitives.assumptions: Neural effort correlates with perceived direction; muscle paralysis decouples M from D.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When M = 0 but W > 0, D remains misattributed.

primitives.assumptions: I remains fixed under voluntary effort; O is misattributed due to E error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E ≠ 0 but I = constant, O becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: GSI probabilistic inference of O using I and assumed E; GSE perceptual update of object location.

primitives.name: Proprioceptive Feedback Futility
primitives.verbatim_quote: But all these feelings are too faint and vague to be of use in the perception of direction.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'proprioceptive signal strength (arbitrary units)', 'T': 'threshold for directional discrimination'}
primitives.assumptions: P < T implies unreliable directional feedback.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P → 0 ⇒ D becomes dependent on non-local cues.

layer2.mapping: GSI rejection of low-confidence proprioceptive inputs; GSE fallback to alternative sensory modalities.
layer2.telemetry: Signal-to-noise ratio in proprioceptive channels during voluntary movement.
